Sujuna Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Sujuna, Georgia

Not demolished. One of two adjacent Jewish cemeteries in Sujuna, a village in western Georgia's Samegrelo-Zemo Svaneti region. Sources disagree on when Jews first settled here - some cite the 11th-12th centuries, others a late-17th-century migration from Lailashi via Bandza; an 1770 document records Jewish serfs gifted to a local church. By the mid-19th century, about 75 Jewish merchants were active in regional trade, and a stone synagogue (built 1819) drew around 100 worshippers on holidays by the mid-20th century. This older cemetery's entrance sign claims use from 1830 to 1990, though legible tombstone dates actually span the mid-19th century to 1966. It was cleaned and fenced in 2013.
